subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides is called a:
questions.explain: A trapezium is defined as a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides.

questions.q: An angle that is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees is described as:
questions.explain: An obtuse angle lies strictly between 90 degrees and 180 degrees.

questions.q: A polygon with eight sides is called a(n):
questions.explain: An octagon is a polygon with eight sides.

questions.q: The angles on a straight line add up to:
questions.explain: Angles on a straight line always sum to 180 degrees.

questions.q: The angles around a point (a full turn) add up to:
questions.explain: Angles around a point make a complete turn of 360 degrees.

questions.q: The sum of the interior angles of a pentagon is:
questions.explain: Using (n - 2) x 180 with n = 5 gives 3 x 180 = 540 degrees.

questions.q: Each interior angle of a regular hexagon measures:
questions.explain: The interior angles sum to (6 - 2) x 180 = 720, so each is 720 / 6 = 120 degrees.

questions.q: Each exterior angle of a regular decagon (10 sides) measures:
questions.explain: The exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360 degrees, so each is 360 / 10 = 36 degrees.

questions.q: The straight line that divides an angle into two equal parts is called the:
questions.explain: An angle bisector cuts an angle into two equal halves.

questions.q: To construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment with compasses, you draw arcs from:
options: Both endpoints using the same compass radius
questions.explain: Equal arcs from both endpoints intersect at points equidistant from each end, defining the perpendicular bisector.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explain: A square has four lines of symmetry: two through midpoints of sides and two along its diagonals.

questions.q: The order of rotational symmetry of an equilateral triangle is:
questions.explain: An equilateral triangle maps onto itself three times in a full turn.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a parallelogram (that is not a rectangle or rhombus) have?
questions.explain: A general parallelogram has no lines of symmetry, only rotational symmetry of order 2.

questions.q: Two similar shapes always have:
questions.explain: Similar shapes have equal corresponding angles and sides in the same ratio, but not necessarily equal lengths.

questions.q: Two similar triangles have a linear scale factor of 3. The ratio of their areas is:
questions.explain: The area scale factor is the square of the linear scale factor, so 3 squared = 9.

questions.q: Two similar solids have a linear scale factor of 2. The ratio of their volumes is:
questions.explain: The volume scale factor is the cube of the linear scale factor, so 2 cubed = 8.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1 : 50 000, a distance of 3 cm represents an actual distance of:
questions.explain: 3 x 50 000 = 150 000 cm, which equals 1.5 km.

questions.q: The angle in a semicircle (subtended by a diameter at the circumference) is:
questions.explain: The angle in a semicircle is always a right angle, 90 degrees.

questions.q: For the same arc, the angle at the centre of a circle compared with the angle at the circumference is:
questions.explain: The angle subtended at the centre is twice the angle subtended at the circumference by the same arc.

questions.q: The angle between a tangent to a circle and the radius at the point of contact is:
questions.explain: A tangent is always perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of contact.
